intro: Scandinavian cool: colourful Nyhavn, design, cycling and New Nordic food.
sights: Renaissance castle with the Crown Jewels.
eat: Glass market halls with food stalls.
arrive: Copenhagen Airport has Metro and trains to the centre (about 15 minutes).
around: Metro, S-trains, buses and harbour buses; cycling everywhere.
pass: City Pass or Copenhagen Card; check current fares.
tip: Rent a bike and stay in the right lane.

intro: A capital built on 14 islands, with a medieval old town, design and archipelago boat trips.
arrive: Arlanda Airport has the Arlanda Express and commuter trains.
around: Tunnelbana metro, trams, buses and commuter ferries all run on SL tickets.
pass: SL travel cards or contactless; check current fares.
tip: Most places are cashless; bring a card.

intro: A green waterfront capital of fjords, Munch and modern architecture.
areas: Karl Johans gate and the Palace.
Opera House and the MUNCH museum.
Cafés, vintage shops and bars by the Akerselva river.
sights: More than 200 sculptures by Gustav Vigeland.
arrive: Oslo Airport Gardermoen has the Flytoget and regional trains.
pass: Ruter tickets and the Oslo Pass; check current fares.
tip: Take a ferry into the Oslofjord on public transport tickets.

intro: A design city on the Baltic, with saunas, islands and a neoclassical centre.
areas: Bohemian district of bars and cafés.
sights: White neoclassical cathedral on Senate Square.
eat: Harbour market with stalls and cafés.
night: Music and arts festival in August.
arrive: Helsinki Airport has trains to the centre (about 30 minutes).
pass: HSL day tickets; the ferry to Suomenlinna is included.
tip: Try a public sauna with a sea dip.

intro: A fairy-tale walled old town, with a digital-savvy, creative modern city around it.
areas: Creative City: former factories with cafés and shops.
eat: Market hall by the train station.
arrive: Tallinn Airport is linked by tram line 4. Ferries arrive from Helsinki.
around: Trams and buses; free for registered residents, paid for visitors.
pass: Tallinn Card or Ühiskaart tickets; check current fares.
tip: Take the day ferry from Helsinki or vice versa.

intro: The Baltics’ biggest city: an art nouveau showcase with a lively medieval centre.
areas: Streets of ornate facades around Alberta iela.
sights: Riga has one of Europe’s richest art nouveau collections.
eat: Herbal liqueur, often mixed with blackcurrant juice.
Smoked fish, rye bread and produce.
night: Bars and clubs in the old town.
Hip street of cafés and bars.
arrive: Riga International Airport is about 10 km from the centre, linked by city bus 22 and taxis. Long-distance buses and trains arrive near the Central Market.
around: Trams, trolleybuses and buses run by Rīgas Satiksme; Old Riga is compact and walkable.
pass: Rīgas Satiksme e-tickets; check current fares.
tip: Old town bar touts: check prices before ordering.

intro: A baroque old town, quirky Užupis and a laid-back, green capital.
areas: New Town with cafés and bars.
eat: Historic market hall with food stalls.
night: Cafés and bars by the river.
Arts venue for gigs and events.
arrive: Vilnius Airport is linked by train and bus.
around: Buses and trolleybuses; the Old Town is walkable.
pass: Vilnius Pass or e-tickets; check current fares.
tip: Read the Užupis constitution on the wall.

intro: Poland’s royal city: a huge market square, Wawel Castle and a lively Jewish quarter.
sights: One of Europe’s largest medieval squares.
eat: Dumplings with savoury or sweet fillings.
Kraków’s ring-shaped bread from street carts.
night: Clubs and bars in medieval cellars.
arrive: Kraków Airport (Balice) has a train link to Kraków Główny station, about 20 minutes. Trains run to Warsaw and across Poland.
around: Trams and buses run by MPK; the Old Town and Kazimierz are easy to walk.
pass: Time-based and 24-hour MPK tickets, bought from machines or apps; validate on boarding.

intro: A resilient capital: a rebuilt old town, Chopin and a dynamic modern city.
eat: Budget canteens serving Polish home cooking.
Food hall in a restored market.
night: Clubs and bars in the centre.
arrive: Warsaw Chopin Airport is linked by train and bus.
tip: Free Chopin concerts in Łazienki on summer Sundays.

intro: A Hanseatic port city with colourful gabled houses, amber and Solidarity history.
sights: Museum of the Second World War
Large museum on the war’s impact.
Seaside resort with a long pier.
arrive: Gdańsk Airport is linked by train and bus.
around: Trams, buses and SKM trains to Sopot and Gdynia.
tip: Take the SKM train to Sopot for the beach.

intro: A compact Danube capital with a hilltop castle and an easy-going old town.
areas: Compact centre of squares and lanes.
The castle and views over the Danube.
Modern riverfront with shops and restaurants.
sights: Hilltop castle with views to Austria and Hungary.
Ruins above the meeting of the Danube and Morava.
Art nouveau Church of St Elizabeth.
eat: Potato dumplings with sheep cheese and bacon.
From vineyards just outside the city.
night: Pubs and cocktail bars in the centre.
Bars along the Danube in summer.
arrive: Bratislava Airport is linked by bus; Vienna Airport is about 45 minutes away.
around: Trams, trolleybuses and buses; the Old Town is small and walkable.
pass: Short-term tickets from machines or via the IDS BK app; check current fares.
tip: Combine Bratislava and Vienna on one trip.

intro: A green, walkable capital of dragons, bridges and riverside cafés.
areas: Cafés and bars along the river.
Alternative culture centre in a former barracks.
sights: Art nouveau bridge with the city’s dragon symbol.
Island church and castle, about an hour away.
eat: Friday street-food market in spring to autumn.
arrive: Ljubljana Airport is linked by shuttle and bus.
around: The centre is largely car-free and walkable; LPP city buses and the castle funicular cover the rest.
pass: Urbana card for buses and the funicular; the Ljubljana Card adds attractions.
tip: Take a boat trip on the Ljubljanica.

intro: Croatia’s capital: Austro-Hungarian grandeur, quirky museums and lively café culture.
areas: Historic hilltop quarter with churches and museums.
Café and bar street below the Upper Town.
sights: Famous for its coloured tiled roof.
Objects and stories from ended relationships.
Open-air market above the main square.
eat: Baked or boiled dough with cottage cheese.
Long coffee sessions on Saturday mornings (špica).
night: Summer clubs and bars by the lake.
arrive: Zagreb Airport is linked by shuttle bus.
around: ZET trams run all over the centre; the funicular links the Lower and Upper Town.
pass: ZET tickets and day tickets; check current fares.
tip: Ride the short funicular between towns.

intro: A city built into a Roman palace, gateway to the Dalmatian islands.
areas: The Roman palace that is the old town itself.
Popular sandy city beach east of the port.
sights: World Heritage Roman palace with the cathedral and cellars.
Forest park with viewpoints and beaches.
Ferries and catamarans to Hvar, Brač and Vis.
Waterfalls and lakes about an hour away.
eat: Meat or octopus slow-cooked under an iron bell (often order ahead).
Fruit and vegetables beside the palace walls.
night: Bars hidden in the old town’s lanes.
Electronic music festival in July (check dates).
arrive: Split Airport is linked by bus. Ferries sail to the islands and Italy.
pass: Buy tickets per journey; check current options.
tip: Book island ferries ahead in summer.

intro: The Pearl of the Adriatic: walled old town, Game of Thrones and island trips.
areas: Walled World Heritage city of marble streets.
Hotels, beaches and promenades west of the centre.
Wooded island a short boat ride away.
sights: Walk the full circuit of the walls (ticketed).
Views over the Old Town and islands.
Nature reserve with peacocks and a botanical garden.
The Old Town’s polished main street.
eat: From the bay of Mali Ston, about an hour away.
night: Bars tucked into the lanes and squares.
Cliffside bars outside the city walls.
arrive: Dubrovnik Airport (Čilipi) is about 20 km south; airport shuttle buses meet flights and run to the Old Town and bus station.
around: Libertas city buses link the Old Town, Gruž port and Lapad; the Old Town itself is pedestrian.
pass: The Dubrovnik Pass bundles the walls, museums and bus travel; check current options.
tip: Walk the walls early to avoid heat and crowds.

intro: A big, lively capital of belle époque boulevards, a vast palace and great nightlife.
areas: Pedestrian streets packed with bars, clubs and restaurants.
Grand avenue of palaces, museums and cafés.
Large lakeside park in the north of the city.
sights: One of the world’s largest administrative buildings; guided tours.
Domed concert hall, home of the George Enescu Philharmonic.
Small, ornate 18th-century church in the Old Town.
eat: Cabbage rolls with sour cream and polenta.
Fried doughnuts with sour cream and jam.
night: The Old Town’s bars and clubs, busy every night.
Electronic music clubs with international DJs.
arrive: Henri Coandă Airport is linked by train and bus.
around: Metro, trams and buses; ride-hailing is common.
pass: STB and Metrorex cards; check current fares.
tip: Use ride-hailing apps rather than street taxis.

intro: An affordable Balkan capital of golden domes, mineral springs and mountain views.
areas: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral and the ancient Serdica ruins.
Pedestrian street of shops and cafés, with mountain views.
Leafy residential district with bars and restaurants.
sights: Hiking and skiing on the city’s doorstep.
World Heritage monastery, about two hours away.
eat: Filo pastry with cheese, a breakfast staple.
Tomato, cucumber and grated white cheese.
night: Cafés and bars along the main street.
arrive: Sofia Airport’s Terminal 2 has a Metro station (line 4) to the centre. Trains and buses link to Plovdiv and beyond.
around: Metro, trams, trolleybuses and buses; the centre is walkable.
pass: Metro and city tickets; check current fares.
tip: Drink from the mineral springs near the Banya Bashi mosque.
